response_text: For users, cooperative multitasking requires threads to yield at good points; in pre-emptive multitasking they don’t have to, since the OS time-slices automatically (they can still yield to be courteous). For the OS, pre-emptive mode tracks a time slice and remaining budget per thread; each tick decrements the budget and, on zero, requests a switch and refreshes the budget. Cooperative mode switches only on yield or blocking; if a pre-emptive thread yields, it’s handled like a normal switch and the slice is refreshed.\n
